title: The Censor Board Took Its Scissors to Welcome To The Jungle. Fourteen Cuts Later, Akshay Kumar's Comedy Limps Into Friday.
excerpt: Bikini visuals gone, 'Paani of Kashmir' deleted, 'Azarudden' swapped for 'Allaudin', and a vulgar hand gesture replaced with a close-up of Vindu Dara Singh. The CBFC has spoken — and the Welcome boys arrive June 26 a little tamer than they shot.
body:
The trailer promised chaos. The censor board promised order. As is tradition in Hindi cinema's longest-running game of tug-of-war, the censor board won — fourteen times over.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=R704yP3dlXw</youtube>

With just days to go before **Welcome To The Jungle** storms into cinemas on June 26, the Central Board of Film Certification has handed the third chapter of the beloved **Welcome** franchise its certificate — a U/A 16+ — but only after a list of demands that reads like a comedy in its own right. Fourteen changes. Some surgical, some baffling, all revealing.

https://x.com/SacnilkEntmt/status/2068988500834435395

Let's start with the part the marketing team would rather you forget. The cut list, as reported exclusively by **Bollywood Hungama**, instructed the makers to delete and replace "sensual bikini visuals, close-up of woman hip passing visuals and hip movement visuals in the song wherever they occurred." At one point it gets specific: the sensual visuals of **Disha Patani** and **Jacqueline Fernandez** have been deleted. The two actresses are among the franchise's biggest draws, their glamour a load-bearing pillar of the film's entire pitch — and the board went straight for it. The song that was built to be the reel-bait of the summer arrives a few degrees cooler than it left the edit bay.

And then there is the genuinely surreal. A "vulgar" hand gesture was not simply blurred or trimmed — it was replaced with a close-up shot of **Vindu Dara Singh**. Read that again. Somewhere in a Mumbai editing suite, an offending gesture has been swapped out for the face of Vindu Dara Singh, which may be the single most Welcome-franchise sentence ever written. If you were designing a meme to summarise Indian film censorship in 2026, you could not improve on it.

The verbal edits are where the politics peek through. A dialogue mentioning **'Paani of Kashmir'** was ordered deleted outright. The line *'Yaad karo kurbani, munh mein bhar lo paani'* was rewritten to *'Jo shaheed hone ja raha tha, uske munh mein bhar lo paani.'* The word **'Gorkha Regiment'** vanished, replaced with the limp *'Tum army se ho?'*. Every **'General'** in the film was demoted to 'Officer' or 'Sir'. The military, it seems, must not be named too precisely, even in a slapstick comedy.

The rest is the board's usual word-policing, and it is gloriously petty. **'Azarudden'** — yes, a passing reference clearly riffing on the cricketer's name — was swapped for **'Allaudin'**. The insult *'andha'* (blind) became *'dheela'* (loose). The line *'Kaala paida hua hai, koyla hai'* was softened to *'saadah paida hua hai, namoona hua hai.'* The phrase *'desh ki tatti'* was deleted, 'screwed' was scrubbed twice, and a 10-second chunk containing the words *'na diya'* was cut clean. After all of it, the film clocks in at exactly 164 minutes and 50 seconds — 2 hours, 44 minutes and change of certified, sanitised mayhem.

Here is the thing the CBFC keeps refusing to learn. We are living in the era of **Animal**, of **Dhurandhar**, of streaming shows where graphic everything is consumed by the crore. Audiences have been conditioned to expect that what they buy a ticket for is the whole thing — and when it isn't, they don't stay home quietly. They go online. The board's own recent history proves it: the cuts to the Hollywood horror **Obsession** earlier this year sent a wave of viewers toward pirated, uncut versions and turned the censorship itself into the story. For a mass-market comedy banking on family footfalls and repeat viewing, a song that's been visibly trimmed is exactly the kind of thing that gets dissected frame-by-frame on social media within hours of release.

None of this, to be clear, dents the film's box-office case. **Welcome To The Jungle** is one of 2026's most anticipated releases for a reason — eighteen years of franchise nostalgia, a sprawling ensemble led by **Akshay Kumar** and **Suniel Shetty**, with Arshad Warsi, Raveena Tandon, Lara Dutta, Paresh Rawal, Johnny Lever and roughly half of Bollywood's comic bench packed in behind them, all directed by Ahmed Khan. The diaspora is precisely the audience this kind of unapologetic big-screen masala is built for. Expect packed houses in Edison, Hounslow and Brampton, where the Welcome brand still means a guaranteed Friday-night outing.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZ4F_lBN7Ro/

It releases worldwide on June 26 — in cinemas, with an eye on an eventual streaming home — fourteen cuts lighter, a Vindu Dara Singh close-up heavier, and exactly as loud as the franchise has always promised to be. The censor board can take the bikini visuals. It was never going to take the noise.
